script.title: Shares vs Debentures: owner or lender?
script.caption_hook: Owner or lender? Shares vs Debentures in one minute

lines.say: Ma'am, shares and debentures both raise money. So what's the difference?
Simple. A shareholder is an owner. A debenture holder is only a lender.
So owners get profit, and lenders get interest?
Exactly. Shareholders get dividend, only if declared. Debenture holders get interest as agreed.
Even if the company makes a loss?
Yes. Interest is a contractual liability to a creditor, so it's payable even in a loss. Dividend needs profit.
And voting? Who gets a say in meetings?
Equity shareholders vote. Debenture holders have no voting right. Remember: Shares Say, Debentures Debt.
Oh! And if the company shuts down, who's paid first?
Debenture holders, as creditors, are paid first. Shareholders are paid after all creditors.
So owner takes risk, lender takes priority!
Right! Debentures are also often secured by a charge on assets. Shares have no such charge.
Remember: owner takes risk, lender takes priority.

check_notes: Checker: Line 8 board ('Shares: can vote'): too broad. Under Section 47, only equity shareholders have general voting rights. Preference shareholders vote only on resolutions that directly affect their rights, or when their dividend is unpaid for two years or more. Correct version: 'Equity shares: can vote' (or 'Shares: vote (preference: limited)'). Also say that Section 71(2) bars the issue of debentures with voting rights.

Checker: Line 6 ('Dividend needs profit'): under Section 123, dividend can be paid out of current profits, past undistributed profits or free reserves, subject to the Companies (Declaration and Payment of Dividend) Rules. So a company can declare a dividend in a loss year out of free reserves. Correct version: 'Dividend can be paid only out of profits or free reserves, and only if declared.'

Checker: Line 10 / Line 13 board ('Paid first' / 'Lender: first'): this is only true relative to shareholders. On winding up, debenture holders do not rank first overall. Secured debenture holders rank with workmen's dues after insolvency or winding-up costs (Sections 326/327, IBC Section 53). Unsecured debenture holders rank as unsecured creditors, after preferential payments. Preference shareholders are also repaid before equity shareholders, so 'Shares: paid last' applies to equity shares. Correct version: 'Debenture holders are paid before shareholders' and 'Equity: paid last'.
